candidate.answerReason: The parallel lines and doubled angle produce an isosceles triangle after an auxiliary construction. Its side relation gives AB=AD+CD=a+b, matching E.

methods.label: Split the trapezoid into a triangle and a parallelogram
methods.explanation:
The doubled angle suggests splitting \(\angle ADC\) into two equal angles. Write \(\theta=\angle ABC\), so \(\angle ADC=2\theta\). The convex trapezoid has \(0<\theta<90^\circ\).

Draw from \(D\) a ray in the direction from \(C\) to \(B\). Because \(DC\parallel AB\), this ray makes an angle \(\theta\) with \(DC\), placing it inside \(\angle ADC\). It meets \(AB\) at an interior point \(X\): it cannot meet the side \(BC\), to which it is parallel.

The parallel-line angle relations give
\[
\angle CDX=\angle AXD=\theta.
\]
Hence
\[
\angle ADX=2\theta-\theta=\theta.
\]
Triangle \(ADX\) has equal angles at \(D\) and \(X\), so its opposite sides are equal:
\[
AX=AD=a.
\]
Also, \(XB\parallel DC\) and \(DX\parallel BC\), so \(XBCD\) is a parallelogram. Its opposite sides give \(XB=DC=b\). Therefore
\[
AB=AX+XB=a+b.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses only parallel-line angles, the equal-angle criterion for an isosceles triangle, and opposite sides of a parallelogram.

methods.label: Extend the legs to form two isosceles triangles
methods.explanation:
Extending the nonparallel sides lets us use the angle condition in two triangles. Put \(\theta=\angle ABC\), so \(\angle ADC=2\theta\) and \(0<\theta<90^\circ\). Since \(AB\parallel CD\),
\[
\angle DAB=180^\circ-2\theta.
\]
Extend \(AD\) beyond \(D\) and \(BC\) beyond \(C\) to meet at \(P\). The two base angles sum to \(180^\circ-\theta<180^\circ\), so the extensions meet on this side of \(AB\), beyond the parallel segment \(CD\).

In triangle \(ABP\), the angle sum gives
\[
\angle APB
=180^\circ-(180^\circ-2\theta)-\theta
=\theta.
\]
Thus \(\angle ABP=\angle APB\), and their opposite sides satisfy \(AP=AB\).

In the smaller triangle \(DCP\), parallelism gives \(\angle DCP=\angle ABP=\theta\), while \(\angle DPC=\angle APB=\theta\). Equal angles again give equal opposite sides, so \(DP=DC=b\). Since \(D\) lies between \(A\) and \(P\),
\[
a=AD=AP-DP=AB-b.
\]
Therefore \(AB=a+b\), choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses supplementary angles, triangle angle sums, parallel-line angles, and equal-angle isosceles triangles, all elementary Euclidean geometry.

Segment and angle arithmetic support both routes. Parallelogram criteria and properties belong only to the first method; the triangle angle-sum theorem belongs only to the second. These assignments describe the mathematical content rather than establishing learner mastery.

review.mathematicalCheck: The displayed convex configuration and angle D=2θ imply 0<θ<90°. In Method 1, the interior parallel ray gives equal angles at D and X, so AX=AD, while the parallelogram gives XB=CD. In Method 2, the extensions give AP=AB and DP=DC; the established point order gives AD=AP-DP. Both independently prove AB=a+b, choice E.
